analysis: What changed vs the 5:00 AM PT premarket brief: (1) The tape faded — futures swung from flat (~+0.06-0.09% at 5:25am ET) to lower (Dow -0.3%, S&P -0.1%, Nasdaq 100 -0.3% by ~9am ET) off the Nasdaq's second straight record close. (2) Chips bifurcated: memory profit-taking (MU -1%, SNDK -1.2%, DRAM ETF -1.5%) after Tuesday's breakouts vs a fresh quantum rotation — IONQ +12-14% on the first real-time quantum error decoder running on a standard CPU, lifting RGTI/QBTS/QNT, with the Quantum World Congress (Sept 23-25) and a Mizuho bullish initiation as catalysts. (3) Oil's peace-premium unwind partially reversed: Trump's 'annihilate' threat vs Iran ran against the UNGA diplomacy progress and WTI/Brent rebounded (Brent back above $100). (4) Macro headwind repriced: >50% October Fed-hike odds, 10Y at 4.98%, dollar at a two-month high, gold -1.3%. (5) The Muse story split: Instacart (+3%) joined the Muse partner stack (widening distribution) while two fresh HN threads added a trust/security counter-narrative (6.8GB sandbox export, Ars 0-day) hours before the Connect keynote. (6) Financials steadied premarket after the 'Muse malaise' -2% day — bounce-or-follow-through is the sub-story at the open. Signal: quantum catalyst, macro repricing, Connect keynote tonight. Noise: the WOR/KB Home single-name moves, the Gemini sandbox single-source item (carried, still fragile).

community_signals.takeaway: A user got Muse to export its own sandbox into a 6.8GB archive (internal docs, integration code, memory records, startup scripts). HN is split: one camp calls it a sandbox-boundary/data-handling failure hours before the Connect keynote, the other says it was the user's own sandbox and the excitement is overblown. Adds a data-privilege skepticism angle to the Muse launch that headlines don't cover. 316 points, ~153 comments.
community_signals.title: I asked Meta's Muse for its filesystem and it sent me 6.8GB

community_signals.takeaway: Ars Technica reported a Muse zero-day; HN discussion focuses on macOS keychain/sandbox protections and a general 'Meta app with near-admin privileges, of course it has zero-days' sentiment. Adds a product-security risk frame around the flagship AI agent on the eve of the keynote. 119 points, ~48 comments.
community_signals.title: Meta's Muse has a serious 0-day

community_signals.takeaway: Beyond the headline: HN digs into the economics — agents don't click ads or react to lightning deals, so Amazon's ad funnel is threatened; there's no standard way to distinguish benign agents from industrial-scale scraping, so sites just block known datacenter IPs. Frames this as the first real platform conflict of the agentic-commerce era, with implications for how Muse could ever be monetized. 151 points, ~158 comments. (Re-verified this run.)
community_signals.title: Amazon blocks Meta's new Muse AI agent from shopping on amazon.com

headlines.headline: Futures faded lower into 9am ET (Investopedia, IBD): Dow -0.3%, S&P 500 -0.1%, Nasdaq 100 -0.3%, after flat-to-slightly-green readings around 5:25am ET — coming off the Nasdaq's second straight record close (27,244.28). 10Y ticked to 4.98%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Record-chase profit-taking plus rising yields dampen opening bids — the open is about Connect tonight and 9:45am ET flash PMIs, not a macro data dump.

headlines.headline: Quantum rally: IonQ +12-14% premarket on its first real-time quantum error decoder that runs on a standard CPU (simulated 408 logical qubits, 31.5M ops, ~0.02% overhead); RGTI +5-6%, QBTS +5%, Quantinuum +4-6.5% followed. Catalysts: Quantum World Congress (Sept 23-25, IonQ/Rigetti CEOs Thursday) and a Mizuho bullish initiation with near-Street-high price targets (MarketWatch, Barron's, TradingKey).
headlines.why_it_matters: A concrete technical milestone (error correction without specialized hardware) revives the commercial-viability thesis — speculative AI-adjacent bid is the session's rotation counterpart to memory profit-taking.

headlines.headline: Memory consolidation: MU -1% premarket after decisively breaking a cup-with-handle buy point at 1,042.40 with Tuesday's 5% rally; SNDK -1.2% after Tuesday's 6.8% rally past a 1,807.38 buy point; DRAM ETF -1.5%, SOXX -1%; AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm also fell (IBD, Barron's).
headlines.why_it_matters: Breakout digestion, not reversal — normal until names lose their buy points; four-day win streaks make them the obvious place for pre-open profit-taking.

headlines.headline: Financials steadying premarket: JPM and SCHW marginally higher after Tuesday's 'Muse malaise' (Financials index -2%, worst day since March; SCHW -6.1%, LPL -7.5%); Uber and Airbnb also steadied (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: Bounce watch: whether the AI-disruption selloff holds or mean-reverts sets the tape's sub-story at the open.

headlines.headline: Earnings movers premarket: Worthington (WOR) +16% after Q1 adjusted earnings and revenue beat LSEG estimates, driven by data-center cooling tank demand; KB Home lower on Q4 delivery guidance below expectations and 16-16.6% margins vs 17.2% expected; Six Flags +1.1% as activist Jana Partners pushes for a sale (WSJ via Barron's, tradersunion).
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-name earnings dispersion confirms the tape is stock-picker's tape today — data-center capex demand is the one clean throughline.

headlines.headline: Microsoft +0.8% premarket; BNP Paribas maintained a $549 price target after talks with Microsoft IR — Azure re-accelerated above 40%, driven by compute expansion and efficiency gains, with higher renewal pricing as a future driver (TradingKey).
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh analyst corroboration of Azure re-acceleration keeps the cloud bid warm into Connect and the PMIs.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -1% premarket (IBD), threatening to snap a six-day winning streak after Tuesday's +0.66% close at $228.18 (52-wk high $236.54); AI server bid intact — SMCI +1.1%, Dell +0.9% premarket (Barron's).
headlines.why_it_matters: Mild digestion in the AI bellwether after six green sessions — not a thesis change; watch the $236.54 high for resistance.

headlines.headline: Apple +0.4% premarket, closing in on a cup-base entry at 344.57 (IBD); record $339.75 close Tuesday, $4.96T cap, intraday print above $5T.
headlines.why_it_matters: Milestone attention pulls flow/haven bids — a close above $342.602 cements the first $5T close.

headlines.headline: Meta flat premarket ahead of tonight's Connect keynote (7pm ET / 4pm PT); Meta officially names AI, AI glasses, VR as the agenda; BofA's Justin Post watching Muse engagement metrics and Muse Spark model updates; options price a ±4.5% move into end of week (Investopedia, AFP).
headlines.why_it_matters: The week's defining catalyst for the Muse trade — engagement/roadmap reveals can extend or deflate the AI-adoption rally.

headlines.headline: Maplebear (Instacart) +3% after adding Meta's AI agent Muse to its grocery platform (CNBC via tradersunion) — the Muse partner stack keeps widening alongside PayPal, Shopify, Expedia.
headlines.why_it_matters: Each partnership widens Muse's distribution and validates the agent-commerce thesis Amazon is resisting — headline read is Muse adoption, not Instacart fundamentals.

headlines.headline: Oil rebounded: WTI $90.70 (+0.2%), Brent $100.30 (+1.1%) back above $100 (Investopedia; Barron's had Brent +0.49%), as Trump's 'annihilate' threat vs Iran undercut the UNGA diplomacy progress; the Saudi East-West pipeline restart still cushions supply.
headlines.why_it_matters: Brent back above $100 re-inserts energy-inflation risk into the premarket — mixed signals mean headline risk is two-sided.

headlines.headline: Rate-hike repricing: traders see slightly >50% odds of an October Fed hike (TradingKey); dollar index at a two-month high; 10Y at 4.98%; gold slumped ~1.3% to ~$4,302, miners FCX -1.4%, NEM -1.8% (TradingKey, Barron's).
headlines.why_it_matters: Hawkish repricing plus a strong dollar is a broad risk-asset headwind into the open — the Fed (hiked last week) hasn't tamed hike chatter.

headlines.headline: Xi arrives in Washington today for the state visit; White House talks and Thursday's state dinner with Cook, Huang, Altman (Reuters); Xi is also expected to meet GM, Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla execs.
headlines.why_it_matters: Optics day — framed as status-quo ceremony, which lowers both catalyst and disappointment risk; keeps AI/trade headline flow alive into tomorrow.
